'''Wakoná''' (Aconã) is an extinct and unattested, presumed language of eastern Brazil, formerly spoken by the Aconã people.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ministério Publico Federal - <nowiki>http://www.mpf.mp.br/</nowiki> |title=Indígenas Aconã recebem FPI do São Francisco com a dança sagrada do Toré, em Traipu |url=https://www.mpf.mp.br/al/sala-de-imprensa/noticias-al/indigenas-acona-recebem-fpi-do-sao-francisco-com-a-danca-sagrada-do-tore-em-traipu |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522154346/https://www.mpf.mp.br/al/sala-de-imprensa/noticias-al/indigenas-acona-recebem-fpi-do-sao-francisco-com-a-danca-sagrada-do-tore-em-traipu |archive-date=2024-05-22 |access-date=2025-04-11 |work=MPF |language=pt-BR }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=editorfpi |date=2024-05-10 |title=Indígenas Aconã recebem FPI AL com a dança sagrada do Toré |url=https://fpisaofrancisco.inf.br/index.php/2024/05/10/indigenas-acona-recebem-fpial/ |access-date=2025-04-11 |language=pt-BR}}</ref> The dispersed ethnic population numbered an estimated 500 to 1,000 in 1995.
== Geographical distribution ==
Wakoná was originally spoken around Lagoa Comprida and in [[Penedo, Alagoas|Penedo]].<ref name="Loukotka"/> Loukotka (1968) reported that the remaining ethnic descendants who speak only Portuguese could be found in the city of [[Porto Real do Colégio]].<ref name="Loukotka">{{cite book |last=Loukotka |first=Čestmír |authorlink=Čestmír Loukotka |title=Classification of South American Indian languages |url=https://archive.org/details/classificationof0007louk |url-access=registration |publisher=UCLA Latin American Center |year=1968 |location=Los Angeles}}</ref> They lived near [[Palmeira dos Índios]] according to Meader (1978).<ref name="Meader-Nordeste">{{cite book |last=Meader |first=Robert E. |url=https://www.silbrazil.org/resources/archives/16988 |title=Indios do Nordeste: Levantamento sobre os remanescentes tribais do nordeste brasileiro |year=1978 |publisher=[[SIL International]] |location=Brasilia |lang=pt |archive-date=2024-10-08 |access-date=2020-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008181259/https://www.silbrazil.org/resources/archives/16988 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
